scope: Theorem 13.5 (Common levels for all finite depths) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 114. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: With the fixed data of either application and the constructions proved in the preceding sections, there is an unbounded class of countable-cofinality strong limit cardinals at which all its finite-depth conclusions hold simultaneously. In the marked application this includes the working packages, projection and type correspondences, amalgamated completion, and exact boundary lifting for every Cn, uniformly over the root prescription codes realized at arbitrarily large eligible single-model levels. In the geometric application it includes categoricity, the working packages, basis lifting, and exact boundary lifting for every finite shape. One such common level may be chosen above any specified set of fixed cardinal thresholds.
